_comment: SANITIZED EXAMPLE. The real reconcile-pairings.json is gitignored and per-machine (it holds absolute repo and vault paths). Only the machine that runs the shared reconcile job needs it: copy this to ~/.claude/state/reconcile-pairings.json, fill the placeholders, and add one pair per project the reconciler should watch. Other machines need none of this. Placeholders: __HOME__ = your home dir; __VAULT_OPS__ = a folder in your Obsidian vault; __NAMESPACE__ = your launchd label namespace; __CODE_ROOT__ = absolute path to your code root (e.g. /Users/you/dev), used verbatim as the probes' cwd (no ~ or $VAR expansion), so it must be absolute.

pairs.heading: ## ⚙️ Built State: derived from ~/.claude
pairs.header_note:
> [!info] Machine-written, do not hand-edit
> Filesystem inventory of `~/.claude` on {today}. Its code lives in the `~/.organism` git repo (symlinked in), pinned to commit `{head}`; a change that rode in on a commit/pull is intended, while an unexplained one (a hook/agent/command added or removed with no new commit) alarms in the reconcile queue. The prose above this fence is yours and is never machine-edited.

hooks.cmd:
ls hooks/*.sh hooks/*.py hooks/*.js 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sort | tr '
' ' '

hook_count.cmd: ls hooks/*.sh hooks/*.py hooks/*.js 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '

commands.cmd:
ls commands/*.md 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/.md$//' | sort | tr '
' ' '

_job_freshness_sample._comment: DISABLED PATTERN, kept OUTSIDE probes:/guards: on purpose: the engine executes every entry in those maps, so a sample parked inside them would run. Why: the launchd probe above only proves agent LABELS are loaded: a job that logs FATAL and exits 0 every day still lists identically, so silent job death is invisible to the self-watch. This pattern makes it visible via the last-success markers (~/.claude/state/<job>-last-success, written only on a confirmed-good run). To arm it: merge 'probes' below into the pair's probes:, 'guards' into guards:, append 'row' to rows:. The probe is volatile (the dates advance daily; display only, never alarms); the GUARD does the alarming: it trips when the daily marker's age exceeds 2 days, flipping the row to UNVERIFIED and raising a machine alarm exactly once on the fresh-to-stale transition.

row.evidence: `~/.claude/state/<job>-last-success`, read {job_freshness__at}: a silently dying job goes stale here

footer: *Drift here (a hook/agent/command added or removed, or the global hook unset) raises an alarm.*

pairs._comment: REPO-CENSUS pair: one git-state row per repo under your code root, rendered onto the census page. Pattern: repo = your code root (git:false → always re-probe; probes are cheap git one-liners). DORMANT repos get non-volatile probes (any transition, such as a new commit or a dirtied tree, alarms: frozen means frozen). ACTIVE repos get volatile probes (display-only; give them their own bespoke pair for semantic alarms). The non-volatile 'inventory' probe alarms when a repo appears or vanishes, which is what keeps the repo watch complete as repos come and go.
pairs.heading: ## ⚙️ Built State: one row per repo under the code root
pairs.header_note:
> [!info] Machine-written section, do not hand-edit
> Repo census taken {today} from the code root: one line of git state per managed repo. Dormant rows are pinned (any change alarms); active rows are display-only. Line format: `HEAD date · commits · tree state (· ↑unpushed,: = no upstream)`.

r_active_example.cmd: h=$(git -C my-active-repo log -1 --format='%h %ad' --date=short 2>/dev/null) || h='⚠️ no git'; c=$(git -C my-active-repo rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '?'); n=$(git -C my-active-repo status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); s=clean; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && s="${n} dirty"; u=$(git -C my-active-repo rev-list --count '@{u}..HEAD' 2>/dev/null || echo '—'); echo "$h · ${c}c · $s · ↑$u"

r_dormant_example.cmd: h=$(git -C my-dormant-repo log -1 --format='%h %ad' --date=short 2>/dev/null) || h='⚠️ no git'; c=$(git -C my-dormant-repo rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '?'); n=$(git -C my-dormant-repo status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); s=frozen; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && s="⚠️ ${n} uncommitted"; echo "$h · ${c}c · $s"

rows.evidence: directory census, read {inventory__at}: a repo appearing or vanishing here alarms
display-only; give active repos their own bespoke pair for semantic alarms
